neighbours.label: the '-cock' (and similar 'ch'/'cy') word piece inside a rare split name such as Bab|cock, Kil|cock, col|ch|icine, coc|cy|x: a spelling-unit pole for a velar 'k/ch' piece mid-word, not the same sentences with names lacking the piece
fire: The orchard was planted by a farmer named Woodcock in 1890.
Our new neighbour, Mrs Glasscock, keeps three goats in the yard.
The paper was written by Adcock and two of her students.
Every summer the Laycock family rents the same cottage by the sea.
The plaque honours the pilot Alcock, who crossed the Atlantic.
In autumn the gardener planted colchicum bulbs under the apple trees.
The village of Haycock has one shop and a small chapel.
After the crash, the doctor said she had bruised her coccyx badly.
quiet: The orchard was planted by a farmer named Wood in 1890.
Our new neighbour, Mrs Glass, keeps three goats in the yard.

Every summer the Lawson family rents the same cottage by the sea.
The plaque honours the pilot Brown, who crossed the Atlantic.
